title: Set up CI: lint + mock-backend test suite on every PR
description: PR #1 (our first outside contribution) merged with zero automated checks — the repo has no CI at all. Now that external contributors exist, every PR should at minimum run 'just lint' and the mock-backend test suite. The obstacle is the OpenFHE C++ build (~heavy); solve with a cached Docker layer or prebuilt artifact containing OpenFHE + liboqs so the per-PR cost is cargo build + tests (~minutes). Stretch: a nightly/weekly job that runs the lattice-backend e2e (~3 min) since it is too slow for every PR. Note tests must run with --test-threads=1 (OpenFHE global state). The existing .cargo/config.toml LIBCLANG_PATH pin (/usr/lib/llvm21/lib) is Linux-shaped and should work in the CI container, but verify against the chosen base image.

title: Guard remaining OpenFHE FFI entry points against C++ exceptions
description: PR #1 (javruben) wrapped the four deserialize_* functions in wrapper.cc with try/catch so corrupt input no longer aborts the process. The remaining FFI entry points that call into OpenFHE are still unguarded: create_bfv_context, keygen, make_packed_plaintext, encrypt, decrypt, generate_recrypt_key, recrypt, and the serialize_* functions. Any C++ exception thrown inside them (e.g. recrypt/decrypt with a ciphertext or key from a mismatched crypto context, allocation failure) crosses the cxx FFI boundary and calls std::terminate() -> SIGABRT, which Rust cannot catch. Same DoS class as PR #1. Audit each entry point, wrap OpenFHE calls in try/catch, and return null/error sentinels the Rust side maps to FfiError. Consider a shared macro/helper to avoid copy-paste, and tests that feed mismatched-context inputs.
design: Use cxx's native exception support instead of hand-rolled try/catch + null sentinels: declare bridge fns in recrypt-openfhe-sys/src/lib.rs as returning Result<T>, and cxx auto-catches C++ exceptions derived from std::exception (covers OpenFHEException, cereal::Exception, bad_alloc) converting them to Err with the exception message — far better diagnostics than a bare null. Scope: (1) migrate the four deserialize_* fns from PR #1's null-UniquePtr sentinel to Result<T>, preserving the corrupt_input_smoke regression test; (2) convert remaining entry points: create_bfv_context, keygen, make_packed_plaintext, encrypt, decrypt, generate_recrypt_key, recrypt, serialize_*. (3) Define rust::behavior::trycatch with catch(...) so non-std exceptions also map to Err instead of terminate. Update recrypt-ffi callers to propagate the richer error text into FfiError::OpenFhe.
close_reason: All 21 bridge fns now declared Result<T>; rust::behavior::trycatch with catch(...) converts any C++ exception (std and non-std) to Err at the boundary. PR #1's null-sentinel pattern migrated; deserializers also throw on null-inner objects (cereal can produce them without throwing). Verified: sys 3/3, ffi 14/14 + 2 smoke (incl. truncation + bit-flip cases), recrypt-core 39/39, workspace clippy clean.

title: Lattice backend: 96-byte plaintext round-trip drops bits (corrupts KeyMaterial)
description:
LatticeBackend::encrypt + decrypt does not round-trip exactly when plaintext.len() == max_plaintext_size() (96 bytes). About half the bytes come back off by -1. This corrupts HybridEncryptor's KeyMaterial header (version byte 1 → 0) and breaks any CLI encrypt → decrypt with the lattice backend.

## Reproduction

Run the unit-level repro (currently marked #[ignore]):

  cargo test -p recrypt-core --features openfhe \
    pre::backends::lattice::tests::test_lattice_encrypt_decrypt_roundtrip_96_bytes \
    -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture

Or the e2e CLI tests:

  cargo test -p recrypt-e2e-tests --features lattice-tests \
    --test lattice_tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1

## Symptom (from the unit test)

For plaintext[i] = (i * 7).wrapping_add(1), positions 18, 20, 22, 24, ..., 36, then 90, 92, 94 decode as plaintext[i] - 1. Other bytes round-trip cleanly.

## Why this never showed up before

- crates/recrypt-core/src/pre/backends/lattice.rs: existing test_lattice_encrypt_decrypt_roundtrip uses a 19-byte plaintext.
- HybridEncryptor unit tests use MockBackend, not LatticeBackend.
- The legacy bash e2e (tests/e2e/recryption.sh lattice) bails at the disabled 'share create' step before any lattice decrypt runs.
- The Rust e2e harness hardcoded MockBackend everywhere.

## Suspected cause

Likely a BFV plaintext-modulus / CRT packing boundary bug in OpenFHE FFI: the 96-byte plaintext exhausts the configured plaintext space and some coefficients wrap. Investigate:
- recrypt-openfhe-sys: plaintext modulus, ring dimension, packing format.
- recrypt-ffi/src/lib.rs: encrypt_bytes / decrypt_bytes byte→coefficient mapping.
- Possibly need to either (a) raise the BFV parameters so 96 bytes * 8 bits fit safely, or (b) shrink KeyMaterial below the safe boundary.

## Acceptance

- test_lattice_encrypt_decrypt_roundtrip_96_bytes passes (un-ignore it).
- All 4 e2e tests in tests/e2e/tests/lattice_tests.rs pass with --features lattice-tests (un-ignore them).
- Add an additional 95-byte and 96-byte boundary test with a randomized payload (proptest) to lock the fix in.

Tracked alongside recrypt-a78 (lattice e2e harness work).
close_reason: fixed: BFV slot range overflow — encode byte pairs as signed i16 instead of unsigned u16 so values stay in [-32768, 32767], inside OpenFHE's signed plaintext window. Added 95-/96-byte boundary tests and a randomized boundary test in lattice.rs; un-ignored the 4 e2e lattice tests.

title: W2+W3: Wallet envelope reuses recrypt-wire::Identity for identity encoding (alphabetical assertion order, byte-equality with wire format)
description: Audit found wallet's identity encoder in recrypt-cli/src/wallet/envelope.rs:130-172 emits assertions in insertion order (name, created, ed25519-public, ed25519-secret, ml-dsa-*, pre-*) instead of predicate-alphabetical per docs/standards/dcbor-determinism.md §7. The wire crate's identity encoder does it correctly. Two encoders for the same logical type (recrypt.identity) is a spec-drift trap. Fix: have the wallet build a recrypt_wire::Identity for each entry and call its to_envelope_bytes(). The wallet still owns the OUTER wallet envelope (subject + 'identity' assertions); each identity is encoded by the wire crate. Add a byte-equality test asserting wallet identity bytes == wire crate identity bytes for the same content.
close_reason: Wallet envelope refactored to delegate identity encoding to recrypt_wire::Identity. New helpers wallet_to_wire_identity / wire_to_wallet_identity. Removed duplicate identity_to/from_envelope encoders. Bonus: added encoder-side fingerprint validation to recrypt_wire (was decoder-only). New test wallet_identity_bytes_match_wire asserts byte-equality. All 28 wallet tests + 14 wire identity_envelope tests + full wire suite pass.

title: W1: BackendId::Display 'lattice' → 'lattice-bfv' (matches spec + wire crate)
description: The just-shipped wallet writes 'lattice' to disk because BackendId::Display::Lattice in crates/recrypt-core/src/pre/mod.rs:31 emits 'lattice'. But docs/standards/wallet-envelope-format.md:108,134 and crates/recrypt-wire/src/convert.rs:15 use 'lattice-bfv'. FromStr at mod.rs:43-50 already accepts 'lattice'/'pq'/'post-quantum'/'openfhe'; need to also accept 'lattice-bfv' (the canonical form). Change Display to emit 'lattice-bfv'; keep all FromStr aliases for backward compat. Note: any existing on-disk wallets created today would have written 'lattice' but those FromStr aliases will continue to read them.
close_reason: BackendId::Display::Lattice changed from 'lattice' to 'lattice-bfv' (canonical per spec + wire crate). FromStr accepts both 'lattice-bfv' and 'lattice' for backward compat. Wire crate convert.rs::backend_to_string already used 'lattice-bfv' so they now agree.

title: Fix identity show / list bs58-encode of multi-MB PRE pubkey hangs CLI
description: recrypt-cli/src/commands/identity.rs lines 286-288 (and 272-274 for JSON output) base58-encode identity.pre.public for display. For the lattice backend this is a multi-MB OpenFHE key; base58 is O(n²) so 'recrypt identity show' / 'identity list --json' effectively hang (hours of CPU at 98%). Reproduced 2026-04-27 with PID 42393 spinning in bs58::encode_into. This is the same class of violation tracked by recrypt-jtw and recrypt-fil but it bites the user on every list/show with a lattice identity, so it's P1 not P3. Fix per docs/standards/encoding-conventions.md §4: use base64 for keys >256B, base58 for ed25519 (32B). Truncate display strings (existing 'truncate(s, 32)' helper) so the user never sees more than ~32 chars of any key anyway.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 'recrypt identity show' on a lattice identity returns in <500ms. 2) 'recrypt identity list --json' on a lattice identity returns in <500ms. 3) Display: ed25519 pubkey base58 (existing). 4) Display: ml-dsa pubkey, lattice-PRE pubkey base64. 5) All key strings truncated for human-readable output. 6) JSON output includes the *full* encoded value (not truncated) but uses base64 for the multi-KB ones. 7) cargo test -p recrypt-cli --bin recrypt passes. 8) cargo test -p recrypt-e2e-tests identity passes.
close_reason: Display path bs58→base64 for keys >256B per encoding-conventions §4. Verified with lattice identity: identity show returns in 1.73s (was infinite). 15 wallet unit + 5 e2e identity tests pass.

title: Unbounded allocation in OpenFHE/cereal deserialization (memory-amplification DoS)
description:
Found by the recrypt-7gi fuzzer on the very first run (deserialize_public_key, 60s). A 173KB malformed public key drives cereal's polymorphic binary deserialization to read an attacker-controlled length field and attempt a ~2 exabyte allocation (std::string::__grow_by in cereal::polymorphic_detail::getInputBinding, reading a class-name string). Stack bottoms out in Serial::Deserialize -> recrypt_openfhe::deserialize_public_key.

PRODUCTION IMPACT (verified by replaying the crash artifact in a normal non-ASan build): operator new for the absurd size throws std::bad_alloc, which the recrypt-zoc trycatch guard catches -> Err(OpenFHE operation failed: std::bad_alloc). Process survives. So the EXTREME case is already handled.

RESIDUAL RISK: relying on the allocator to reject the size is fragile. An attacker can craft a 'merely huge' length (e.g. 50-200GB) that the allocator may actually try to satisfy, touching pages until the box OOM-kills the recryption proxy — a DoS. Root cause is cereal trusting embedded length fields without bounding them against remaining stream size; affects all four deserialize_* paths (public/private key, ciphertext, recrypt key), not just pubkey.

MITIGATIONS TO EVALUATE:
1. Run the proxy under RLIMIT_AS / a container memory cap so ANY runaway allocation deterministically fails fast as bad_alloc (which we now catch) instead of OOM-killing the host. Cheap, robust, generalizes beyond this one path. Likely the primary fix.
2. Defensive input-size cap at the FFI boundary (legit artifacts: pk ~263KB, ct ~263KB, sk ~132KB, rk ~525KB). NOTE: insufficient alone — the crash input was 173KB yet claimed a 2EB internal length — but cheaply rejects oversized blobs.
3. Investigate whether cereal's PortableBinaryInputArchive size-sanity options or a custom archive can bound per-field allocations against bytes-remaining.

ASAN/FUZZER NOTE: under ASan this is a hard abort (allocation-size-too-big / out-of-memory) regardless of allocator_may_return_null, because cargo-fuzz overrides ASAN_OPTIONS for the run. The fuzz harness needs a fork-mode / known-crash strategy (see recrypt-7gi) to keep finding OTHER bugs past this one.
notes: PRIMARY MITIGATION LANDED (bc758d4): recrypt-server RLIMIT_AS cap (default 16 GiB) converts the runaway allocation into catchable bad_alloc instead of OOM-kill; recrypt-zoc FFI guard already turns that into Err. Locked in by hrq_allocation_bomb_pubkey_returns_err regression test. RESIDUAL (now P2): (1) cheap defensive input-size cap at FFI boundary (reject blobs > largest legit artifact ~525KB); (2) investigate cereal PortableBinaryInputArchive per-field size bounding; (3) macOS ignores RLIMIT_AS — document container memory limit for prod deploys.

title: Make LIBCLANG_PATH pin work on macOS (currently Linux-only)
description: .cargo/config.toml pins LIBCLANG_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm21/lib for the oqs-sys bindgen 0.71 / libclang>=22 incompatibility, but that path is Linux-only. On macOS the path does not exist and oqs-sys builds fail unless the dev manually overrides (e.g. LIBCLANG_PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm@19/lib). Cargo [env] cannot be conditional per-platform, so either: (a) move the pin into the justfile with OS detection, (b) document the macOS override in CLAUDE.md/README and keep force=false so the local env wins, or (c) check whether bumped oqs-sys (bindgen >= 0.72) removes the need entirely — the config comment says the pin is temporary. Prefer (c) if available, else (a).

title: Fuzz the OpenFHE FFI surface (deserializers first)
description: Phase 9 is security-audit prep, and PR #1's bug class (corrupt input -> process abort) is exactly what cargo-fuzz finds mechanically. Add fuzz targets over the four deserialize_* paths (garbage, truncated, and bit-flipped valid serializations), then extend to recrypt/decrypt with structurally-valid-but-mismatched inputs once those entry points are exception-guarded. Blocked on recrypt-zoc: fuzzing unguarded entry points just rediscovers SIGABRT instead of finding new bugs. Wire the corpus into CI as a smoke job (short -max_total_time) with longer runs ad hoc. Note: OpenFHE deserialization is slow per-exec; expect low exec/s — consider a dictionary seeded from valid serializations to reach deeper states.
close_reason: Harness delivered: 4 libfuzzer targets over deserialize_* with seed-corpus generator and fork-mode just recipes. First run found recrypt-hrq (allocation bomb). Extending targets to encrypt/decrypt/recrypt with mismatched-context inputs, and wiring a campaign into CI, are tracked separately (recrypt-g5e for CI).

Also fix stale '.dcyw' strings in 'recrypt config show' and the unknown-key error message in 'recrypt config set' (already done in this session for the .dcyw display fix). title: nj1-D: Rebuild Capability as envelope-native bearer token
description: Rebuild `identikey_storage_auth::Capability` as the project's UCAN/JWT-style bearer token: signed, optionally time-limited, presentable across all surfaces (proxy, storage, future peer-to-peer). Use Gordian Envelope as the container so subject fields and assertions get the dCBOR canonical encoding for free (replaces the hand-rolled domain-tagged TLV in capability.rs:72). Subject identifies the resource (file hash, keyspace id, account fp, or future resource refs); assertions carry permissions, expiry, notes — elidable/salted per wire-protocol §3.7. Delegation: include a `parent` field for signature chains but defer chain-verification logic to a future ticket. Validates AC #4 of nj1 by being the second endpoint to flow through the codegen pipeline established by nj1-B.
design: Open question carried from nj1: how utoipa models bc-envelope's salted/elidable assertions. This issue is where we answer it. Proposal: emit JSON projection as the fully-elaborated form (no elision) and document that envelope/CBOR is the canonical authority; clients reading JSON get the unredacted view.
acceptance_criteria: 1. `Capability` round-trips through Gordian Envelope (dCBOR) with canonical encoding. 2. Single signature path (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-87 multisig) covers the envelope subject + assertions; salted assertions can be elided without invalidating the signature. 3. HTTP issue/verify endpoints generated through the nj1-B codegen pipeline. 4. `signature_payload()` TLV code deleted. 5. Delegation chain field present but unused; documented as future work with a follow-up beads issue. 6. Wire-protocol.md §3.7 reconciled with the implementation.
notes: Parent epic: recrypt-nj1. NOT critical path — current proxy auth uses per-request multisig + AccessGrant lookups, not bearer tokens. This is plumbing for a future offline-verifiable / cross-surface authorization story (UCAN-shaped). Current keyspace-binding in the code is interim; the rebuild generalizes the subject.
close_reason: Capability rebuilt envelope-native: subject + subject-kind generic, salted/elidable assertions (permissions/expires-at/note), wrap-then-sign with raw-bytes signature assertions (ed25519 + optional ML-DSA-87), parent field present for delegation chain (verification deferred). Old TLV signature_payload + DOMAIN_TAG deleted. POST /capabilities/verify endpoint generated through nj1-B codegen pipeline (proves AC #4: second endpoint added in <1 day). dump_openapi gained a 3.1→3.0 nullable transform. wire-protocol.md §3.7 reconciled with implementation. 7 new unit tests + 36 e2e tests pass.

title: nj1-C: Rename MemberCapability → Permission
description: Reclaim the name 'Capability' for the bearer-token type by renaming `MemberCapability` (the permission-tag enum used inside KeyspaceDoc.members) to `Permission`. This is mechanical: rename the type, the column references, the JSON tags (members.capabilities → members.permissions), and update tests/docs. AccessGrant.capabilities field also renames to .permissions. After this lands, `Capability` unambiguously refers to the bearer token, `Permission` is the role/permission tag.
acceptance_criteria: 1. `grep -r MemberCapability` returns 0 hits in src/. 2. KeyspaceDoc canonical_bytes() output is unchanged (the on-wire tag strings 'read'/'write'/etc. don't change). 3. JSON field 'capabilities' on KeyspaceDoc and AccessGrant is renamed to 'permissions' (one breaking wire change — log it as such). 4. All e2e tests pass.
notes: Parent epic: recrypt-nj1. Cleanup precondition for nj1-D. Mechanical rename; no semantic change to permission model. Wire-format break is acceptable per epic decisions: dreamball has not written wire/integration code yet.
close_reason: Renamed MemberCapability → Permission across identikey-storage-auth + recrypt-server (44 sites). Field 'capabilities' renamed to 'permissions' on Member, AccessGrant, Capability, MemberJson, AccessGrantJson, plus the SQL columns keyspace_members.capabilities + grants.capabilities. SQL migration v2→v3 added (ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN), and a pre-existing schema_version row-accumulation bug fixed in passing. Wire JSON field name now 'permissions' (one breaking wire change, allowed per epic decisions). All 36 e2e tests pass.

title: nj1-B: Codegen pilot — POST /accounts end-to-end
description: Migrate `POST /accounts` from hand-written request/response/handler to schema-as-source-of-truth. Replace the hand-written http-api-reference.md section for /accounts with generated content. Existing CLI and server tests still pass against the new schema. 3. http-api-reference.md /accounts section is generated, not hand-written. 4. title: E2E: parameterize harness over PRE backend, add lattice-gated correctness tests
description:
The existing 'e2e' suite hardcodes MockBackend at 3 sites in tests/e2e/src/harness.rs (server config, RECRYPT_BACKEND env, CliRunner ctor) and the api tests construct MockBackend directly. That makes it integration-only — no Rust e2e test exercises the real OpenFHE BFV path. Only the bash script (just test-e2e-lattice, ~3 min) covers lattice.

Plan (mirrors s3-tests feature pattern):
1. Add 'lattice-tests' cargo feature in tests/e2e/Cargo.toml.
2. Add TestHarness::with_backend(BackendId) — keep TestHarness::new() defaulting to mock.
3. Add lattice-gated variants of the 4 crypto-correctness tests (mock versions stay as fast plumbing smoke):
   - test_full_recryption_roundtrip_lattice (api_share_tests) — decrypt recrypted wrapped key with Bob secret
   - test_encrypt_decrypt_roundtrip_lattice (cli_tests)
   - test_encrypt_empty_file_lattice (cli_tests)
   - test_encrypt_large_file_lattice (cli_tests, possibly smaller payload)
4. Add justfile target: 'just test-e2e-lattice-rust' running with --features lattice-tests --test-threads=1.

Out of scope: keyspaces/grants, signing routes, identity import/export, wallet CLI — those are tracked separately.
close_reason: Harness parameterized over BackendId; lattice-tests feature added; 4 lattice e2e tests + 1 unit-level repro added (all #[ignore]'d on recrypt-fwg). Mock suite stays 36/36 green. Un-ignoring lands with the recrypt-fwg fix.

title: [epic] Phase 9: schema-as-source-of-truth (codegen for JSON+CBOR+REST)
description:
Today recrypt pays a 4-way sync tax: docs/wire-protocol.md ↔ crates/recrypt-wire/* ↔ recrypt-server/routes/* ↔ recrypt-cli/client/api.rs. Three audits in 2026-04-27 surfaced spec/code drift in all three domains (wallet, wire, HTTP). The durable fix: a single Rust-as-IDL schema source whose projections are JSON-REST (via OpenAPI), Gordian Envelope/dCBOR (already what bc-envelope's MultiFormat trait does), and typed clients in TS/Python/Swift.

## Decisions made (don't relitigate)
- IDL: utoipa (axum-native annotations, OpenAPI gen).
- Client generator: progenitor (Rust→Rust+TS, lightweight; no Java toolchain).
- bc-envelope's MultiFormat trait stays as the CBOR projection — it works.
- JSON canonical encoding for bytes: base64 standard (RFC 4648 §4 with padding) per encoding-conventions.md.
- Dreamball has not yet written wire/integration code, so wire-shape compatibility is NOT a constraint. The b64:/b58:/bare-base58 tagged-input convention introduced in recrypt-6aj can be retired once new endpoints emit untagged base64.
- Existing wire types stay as-is for the pilot — recrypt.identity and recrypt.encrypted-file are not getting rewritten just for codegen's sake.

## Acceptance criteria
1. One pilot endpoint ships with all four projections derived from one Rust schema definition: JSON request/response, dCBOR envelope, TS client (via progenitor), OpenAPI spec.
2. http-api-reference.md content for the pilot endpoint is generated, not hand-written.
3. Encoding rules baked in: bytes → base64 in JSON, raw bytes in CBOR, Uint8Array in TS, Vec<u8>/[u8;N] in Rust — no per-field encoding decisions.
4. A second endpoint can follow the pilot in less than one day's work (proves the toolchain scales).

## Suggested pilot
- recrypt.capability (currently hand-rolled domain-tagged TLV in crates/identikey-storage-auth/src/capability.rs:72) — no entrenched JSON shape to preserve, so it's a clean greenfield. Bonus: closes the spec gap from wire-protocol.md §3.7.
- Alternative: POST /accounts (smallest existing endpoint).

## Pointers at current surfaces
- Current JSON shapes: recrypt-cli/src/client/api.rs:303-361.
- Current REST handlers: recrypt-server/src/routes/{accounts,recryption,files,signing,keyspaces}.rs.
- Current OpenAPI-equivalent: docs/http-api-reference.md (hand-written, drifted twice in 2026-04).
- Current envelope encoders: crates/recrypt-wire/src/{identity,convert,impls}.rs.
- Existing MultiFormat trait: crates/recrypt-wire/src/format.rs.
- Capability TLV target for migration: crates/identikey-storage-auth/src/capability.rs.

## Out of scope
- Rewriting recrypt.identity envelope to fit the new pattern (it's working).
- Breaking the on-disk wallet format (recrypt-03y just shipped).
- Reimplementing recrypt.encrypted-file (also working).

## Dependencies
- recrypt-0cz (wallet unknown_assertions forward-compat) is independent.
- recrypt-5um (hybrid identity export) is independent.
- Capability envelope migration is part of THIS epic — best pilot candidate.

## Open questions for the agent picking this up
- Should the wallet's on-disk identity envelope be regenerated from the same schema, or stay separate? Lean: separate, because the wallet has unique constraints (always-secrets-present, raw-bytes per encoding-conventions.md §1).
- How to handle bc-envelope's salted/elidable assertions in the codegen — utoipa won't model these natively.

title: Wire Wallet::save/load through envelope path; bump version to 2
description:

title: Build envelope encode/decode module per spec §3.1, §3.2
description:
New module recrypt-cli/src/wallet/envelope.rs with two functions:
  - to_envelope(&WalletData) -> Result<Vec<u8>>  : encode to dCBOR bytes
  - from_envelope(&[u8]) -> Result<WalletData>   : decode from dCBOR bytes

Wallet envelope shape (spec §3.1):
  - Subject: leaf with map {type: "recrypt.wallet", format-version: 2_u32}
  - Assertions: "active-identity" → string (only if Some); "identity" → nested envelope, repeated once per identity. Self-signatures are deferred.
  - No salting (spec §3.1: 'Salting is unnecessary — the wallet is encrypted at rest').

Identity envelope shape (spec §3.2):
  - Subject: leaf with map {type: "recrypt.identity", format-version: 1_u32, fingerprint: <32 raw bytes>}. NOTE: fingerprint is in the SUBJECT, not an assertion.
  - to_envelope MUST verify fingerprint == Blake3(ed25519-public) before emitting; from_envelope MUST verify the same on load (return error if mismatch).
  - Assertions (raw byte values unless noted): name (string), created (CBOR tag 1 epoch time), ed25519-public, ed25519-secret, ml-dsa-public, ml-dsa-secret, pre-backend (string), pre-public, pre-secret.

Implementation sketch is in spec §10. Confirm bc-envelope's nested-envelope API matches the sketch — if it doesn't, adapt. This is also where any bc-envelope risk surfaces; spike a 1-identity round-trip first if uncertain.

Do NOT wire to Wallet::save/load yet — that's the next bead.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Round-trip unit test inside the new module: WalletData with 1 mock identity → envelope → WalletData; assert byte-equal at the WalletData level. 2) Tampered fingerprint test: build an envelope with fingerprint != Blake3(ed25519-public); from_envelope returns an error. 3) Multi-identity test: 3 identities round-trip; active-identity preserved.
close_reason: envelope.rs encode/decode module landed: WalletData<->dCBOR roundtrip with active-identity assertion + Blake3 fingerprint validation on both encode and decode paths; 9/9 unit tests pass (roundtrip 0/1/3 ids, determinism, tampered fp rejection, wrong type/version rejection, BackendId roundtrip).

title: Convert WalletData/Identity field types to raw bytes
description:
Spec §4: keys inside the encrypted wallet are raw bytes (CBOR major type 2). No base58, no base64. Audit recrypt-cli/src/wallet/format.rs::Identity and any related KeyPair struct: every key field must be Vec<u8> or fixed-size array (e.g. [u8; 32] for ed25519). If anything is currently a base58/base64 String, convert it. Adjust load/save callers as needed.

Decision (per epic design): kill the global-config active-identity fallback. The active_identity field stays Option<String> on WalletData, but the comment 'Falls back to the global config' goes away and so does the actual fallback in load logic if any exists.

This bead is JUST type changes — no envelope work, no version-byte change. The on-disk format (still v1 JSON) keeps working. Existing tests that JSON-serialize raw bytes will need their fixtures regenerated; that's covered in a later bead.
acceptance_criteria: 1) grep -rn 'base58\|base64\|bs58\|BASE64' recrypt-cli/src/wallet/ returns nothing relevant. 2) Identity struct fields are byte types. 3) cargo build -p recrypt-cli is clean. 4) Existing wallet tests still build (passing them is the next bead's problem if fixtures break).

Build clean; tests build (run/regen in .5 + .6). All wallet/* base64 matches are in credential.rs for keychain AEAD-key encoding, not wallet body.

title: Migrate wallet to Gordian Envelope format
description: Replace recrypt-cli's JSON-in-XChaCha20Poly1305 wallet body with a Gordian Envelope (dCBOR) body, sealed by the same Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305 outer shell. Bump the on-disk shell version byte from 1 to 2; reject v1 with a clear error (no migration). All identity key fields move to raw bytes. Spec: docs/standards/wallet-envelope-format.md.
design:
Crate ownership: keep WalletData/Identity in recrypt-cli (wallets are local-only, never on the wire). Add bc-envelope as a DIRECT dependency of recrypt-cli — do NOT depend on recrypt-wire for this; wallet types stay free of wire-protocol concerns.

Active-identity policy: drop the global-config fallback that today's format.rs:25-27 falls back on. Active identity lives ONLY in the wallet envelope as the 'active-identity' assertion (spec §3.1). One source of truth.

Self-signatures (spec §3.1, optional): DEFER. Spec marks them optional and explicitly notes they are not a security boundary. Add later if a use case appears.

Spec section anchors used by child beads: §3.1 top-level wallet envelope; §3.2 identity envelope (note: fingerprint is in the SUBJECT, not an assertion, and MUST equal Blake3(ed25519-public)); §4 raw-byte key encoding; §5 outer-shell layout (offsets and version byte position); §7 v1 rejection error string; §10 implementation sketch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) format.rs VERSION constant is 2. 2) Wallet::load rejects v1 with 'Wallet format v1 is no longer supported. Create a new wallet with recrypt identity new.' 3) Plaintext after AEAD decrypt parses as Envelope with subject {type: recrypt.wallet, format-version: 2}. 4) All identity key fields are raw bytes; no base58/base64 inside the wallet. 5) active-identity is an envelope assertion, not a subject field. 6) Round-trip save→load yields a byte-equal WalletData. 7) RECRYPT_NO_KEYCHAIN=1 and RECRYPT_CONFIG_DIR continue to work. 8) just test-e2e identity CRUD subset passes. 9) No serde_json usage in recrypt-cli/src/wallet/.
close_reason: Epic complete: wallet body migrated from JSON-in-XChaCha20-Poly1305 to Gordian Envelope (dCBOR) wrapped in the same Argon2id+XChaCha20-Poly1305 outer shell, shell version bumped 1→2, v1 rejection emits exact spec'd string before Argon2 derivation. All 7 sub-issues closed. 28 wallet unit tests + 5 identity-envelope integration tests + 17 API E2E + 19 CLI E2E all pass. Spec at docs/standards/wallet-envelope-format.md flipped to Stable.

title: nj1-followup: unify body-byte encoding to base64 across endpoints
description: POST /accounts (recrypt-gpc) kept the legacy ed25519_pk: base58 + ml_dsa_pk: base64 split for body bytes — inconsistent with the epic's 'no per-field encoding decisions' principle. The split exists because ed25519_pk parity-matches fingerprint (which appears as a URL path segment, where base58 is preferred). Decide: (a) all body bytes base64, fingerprints stay base58 in path segments; (b) fingerprints also become base64 (impacts URL aesthetics + every existing path); (c) keep split as documented exception. Recommend (a). Apply across /accounts and any future endpoints; canonical-message templates in http-api-reference.md §1.3 also need updating in lockstep.
notes: Parent epic: recrypt-nj1. Captured during recrypt-gpc commit; documented in CreateAccountRequest schema description.

title: nj1-followup: Capability delegation chain verification
description: recrypt-91h shipped Capability with the wire-format `parent` field present (32-byte digest of the parent capability's wrapped envelope subject) but verification of the chain is not implemented. Today, verifying a capability with `parent` set checks only the immediate signature, not that the issuer was authorized to delegate. Implement: (1) chain walk: given a leaf capability, follow `parent` digests up through a provided pool of parent envelopes; (2) authorization-attenuation check: each step must be issued by the previous step's grantee; (3) permission-attenuation check: child permissions ⊆ parent permissions; (4) optional max depth. Decide where the parent pool lives (HTTP endpoint that resolves digests? client-side bundle?). UCAN's spec is a useful reference.
notes: Parent epic: recrypt-nj1. Delegation is the load-bearing UCAN feature; without chain verification, Capability is functionally equivalent to a single-hop signed token.
close_reason: Implemented bundled bare-digest chain verification per D-3. New capability_chain module with ParentResolver trait + BundledResolver impl, verify_chain walks leaf→root checking signature, granted-to/issuer linkage, Delegate-on-parent, permission subset, subject identity, expiry monotonicity, max depth. 12 tests cover happy path + every rejection case. VerifyingKeys now derives Clone for closure-based key lookups. Decision doc at docs/decisions/2026-04-29-capability-chain-decisions.md.

title: nj1-followup: TypeScript client generator selection (progenitor is Rust-only)
description: Epic recrypt-nj1 listed progenitor as 'Rust→Rust+TS' but progenitor only generates Rust. TS client generation needs a separate tool. Candidates: openapi-typescript (types only), openapi-typescript-codegen (deprecated), orval (full client + react-query), Hey API (modern, actively maintained), openapi-generator (Java toolchain — explicitly ruled out by epic). Recommend Hey API or orval. Distribution choice (sibling crate vs separate npm) folds into recrypt-991 (decision doc).
notes: Parent epic: recrypt-nj1. Rust client path proven by recrypt-gpc.
close_reason: TS client lives at recrypt-client-ts/, generated by @hey-api/openapi-ts (v0.97.0) with @hey-api/client-fetch runtime. Both endpoints (createAccount, verifyCapability) surface as named SDK methods with full types. just openapi-regen now orchestrates Rust client + docs + TS client in one shot. Sibling-directory layout per D-2 (docs/decisions/2026-04-28-codegen-pipeline-decisions.md). Typecheck clean.

title: nj1-followup: progenitor 3.1 OpenAPI support (or downgrade alternative)
description: utoipa 5 emits OpenAPI 3.1.0 but progenitor 0.10 parses via openapiv3 2.x which only supports 3.0.x. The dump-openapi binary currently downgrades the version field to 3.0.3 as a workaround; this works for the empty bootstrap and probably for simple endpoints, but will break the moment we use 3.1-only features (tuple types, exclusiveMinimum as bool, pattern properties, content-type per response). Options: 1) wait for progenitor to support 3.1, 2) switch to a different generator that handles 3.1, 3) write a real 3.1→3.0 transformer (drop unsupported features, downgrade nullable). Decide once nj1-B (POST /accounts pilot) surfaces real schemas.
notes: 2026-04-28: Bumped progenitor 0.10 → 0.14 (current latest, released 2026-04-24). Did NOT gain 3.1 support — progenitor-impl 0.14 still pins openapiv3 = '2.2.0', and openapiv3 v2 only models 3.0.x. The 3.1→3.0 transform in dump_openapi.rs is still required. Real fix awaits openapiv3 gaining 3.1 OR progenitor swapping parser (e.g. to oas3). Workaround handles nullable arrays today; will need to grow if utoipa starts emitting other 3.1-only constructs (tuple types via prefixItems, exclusiveMinimum/Maximum as numbers, type-as-array unions, patternProperties).
close_reason: informational only — no action needed

title: nj1-E: Decision doc — wallet schema separation + TS distribution
description: Capture two decisions surfaced by nj1 as a short doc under docs/decisions/ (or wherever the project keeps ADRs). 1) Wallet on-disk identity envelope: regenerated from the unified schema, or kept separate? Recommendation per epic: separate, because wallet has unique constraints (always-secrets-present, raw-bytes encoding per encoding-conventions.md §1). 2) TS client distribution: sibling crate inside recrypt repo, or separate npm package? Recommendation: sibling crate for now, separate npm later when an external consumer wants it. Doc the rationale and reversal cost for each.

title: Wallet envelope: round-trip unknown assertions for §8 forward-compat

Mirror the pattern in /Users/dukejones/work/Identikey/recrypt/crates/recrypt-wire/src/identity.rs:12-32 + :217-220 + :372-381: KNOWN_PREDICATES const, known_predicate_digests() OnceLock, unknown_assertions: Vec<(Envelope, Envelope)> field on WalletData and Identity, re-emit unknowns in original order on encode. Also document this in the wallet/envelope.rs module docstring.
close_reason: Wallet envelope decoder now collects unknown wallet-level and identity-level assertions into WalletData/Identity unknown_assertions and re-emits them on encode, mirroring the wire crate pattern.
